statement: The function returns a result r. Let ys be the value sequence of r. Let I be the set of all indices i with 0 <= i < n such that for every j with i < j < n, xs[j] <= xs[i]. Let i_0 < i_1 < ... < i_{m-1} be the elements of I in increasing order. Then m = len(ys) and ys[k] = xs[i_k] for every 0 <= k < m. Equivalently, ys is obtained from xs by deleting exactly those entries xs[i] for which there exists j with i < j < n and xs[j] > xs[i], while preserving the relative order of the remaining entries.
preconditions: Let xs be the value sequence of head from left to right and n = len(xs). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000 and 1 <= xs[i] <= 100000 for every 0 <= i < n.

statement: The function returns a result r for every head satisfying the preconditions; it does not panic, overflow, or otherwise fail.
preconditions: Let xs be the value sequence of head from left to right and n = len(xs). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000 and 1 <= xs[i] <= 100000 for every 0 <= i < n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, letting ys be its value sequence, 1 <= len(ys) <= n.
preconditions: Let xs be the value sequence of head from left to right and n = len(xs). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000 and 1 <= xs[i] <= 100000 for every 0 <= i < n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, letting ys be its value sequence, len(ys) >= 1 and ys[len(ys)-1] = xs[n-1].
preconditions: Let xs be the value sequence of head from left to right and n = len(xs). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000 and 1 <= xs[i] <= 100000 for every 0 <= i < n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, letting ys be its value sequence, ys is an order-preserving subsequence of xs: there exist indices 0 <= i_0 < i_1 < ... < i_{len(ys)-1} < n such that ys[k] = xs[i_k] for every 0 <= k < len(ys).
preconditions: Let xs be the value sequence of head from left to right and n = len(xs). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000 and 1 <= xs[i] <= 100000 for every 0 <= i < n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, letting ys be its value sequence, ys is non-increasing: for every k with 0 <= k < len(ys)-1, ys[k] >= ys[k+1].
preconditions: Let xs be the value sequence of head from left to right and n = len(xs). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000 and 1 <= xs[i] <= 100000 for every 0 <= i < n.

statement: Let M be the maximum value of xs and let c be the number of indices i with xs[i] = M. Whenever the function returns a result r, letting ys be its value sequence, len(ys) >= c; for every k with 0 <= k < c, ys[k] = M; and for every k with c <= k < len(ys), ys[k] < M.
preconditions: Let xs be the value sequence of head from left to right and n = len(xs). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000 and 1 <= xs[i] <= 100000 for every 0 <= i < n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, letting ys be its value sequence, ys = xs if and only if xs is non-increasing, meaning that for every i with 0 <= i < n-1, xs[i] >= xs[i+1].
preconditions: Let xs be the value sequence of head from left to right and n = len(xs). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000 and 1 <= xs[i] <= 100000 for every 0 <= i < n.

statement: If xs is non-decreasing, meaning that for every i with 0 <= i < n-1, xs[i] <= xs[i+1], then whenever the function returns a result r, letting ys be its value sequence, ys consists exactly of all occurrences of M = xs[n-1]: if c is the number of indices i with xs[i] = M, then len(ys) = c and ys[k] = M for every 0 <= k < c.
preconditions: Let xs be the value sequence of head from left to right and n = len(xs). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000 and 1 <= xs[i] <= 100000 for every 0 <= i < n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, let ys be its value sequence and match each position k of ys to the unique original index i_k selected by the exact suffix-maximum characterization, so ys[k] = xs[i_k] and the i_k are exactly the indices i with 0 <= i < n and xs[j] <= xs[i] for every j with i < j < n. For every original index i not among these selected indices, there exists a selected index p such that i < p < n and xs[p] > xs[i].
preconditions: Let xs be the value sequence of head from left to right and n = len(xs). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000 and 1 <= xs[i] <= 100000 for every 0 <= i < n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, letting ys be its value sequence, min{ys[k] | 0 <= k < len(ys)} = xs[n-1].
preconditions: Let xs be the value sequence of head from left to right and n = len(xs). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000 and 1 <= xs[i] <= 100000 for every 0 <= i < n.
